brief: Goldman Sachs' positioning monitor argues fixed income demand is holding up despite rising rates. Through most of 2026 investors allocated steadily to fixed income, concentrated in short-term US government bonds, with inflation-protected and structured products also drawing high inflows. Credit fund flows were positive but the gap to sovereigns widened further. Duration exposure stayed elevated: active managers' rate sensitivity became more negative in the US and Euro Area, asset managers' net long in Treasury futures sits close to cycle highs, and risk reduction was concentrated in front-end contracts while long-dated duration-adjusted exposure remained elevated. TLT flows accelerated in August and outpaced IG credit ETFs, and the 1-month CBOT 30-year call-put volume ratio reached around 1-year highs. Flows differentiate regionally, with non-residents turning large net sellers of JGBs at the front end while active funds still favour OATs over Bunds and Gilts despite wider OAT spreads. The sentiment and positioning indicator sits around the 58th percentile and the Risk Appetite Indicator around 1, with VIX and MOVE below their 40th percentile and hedge fund net leverage well below earlier peaks. Outside fixed income, JPY positioning recovers, USD long exposure softens, and gold positioning and ETF flows rise.
